column5: lines($path) with $path a plain Str is real-Raku's Str.lines (splits the string's OWN text), never a file-open -- verified directly against /home/resources/rakudo-local/bin/raku: lines("/tmp/x") on a file that exists WITH real content still returns ("/tmp/x",), not the file's lines; only .IO.lines or a filehandle reads the file. This entry's open($path, ':r') is SCRIP's shared Icon-style open() calling convention (a string mode positional), which real Raku's open() rejects outright (arity error) -- verified equivalent to real Raku's open($path, :r) adverb form, which the oracle runs identically through spurt/slurp/open/slurp/close. The old ref assumed lines($path) re-opens and reads the file; that was never checked against the oracle and was wrong. SCRIP's current output (path string literal, once) is the oracle-correct answer for this exact source, confirmed identical in m3 and m4; the fix that exposed it is SCRIP's by_name_dispatch.c lines() builtin, which used to wrongly fopen() a bare string argument.
